children: CEO John Ternus is reportedly considering a significant overhaul of the iPhone maker's product development strategy, potentially accelerating launches, dismantling rigid release schedules and encouraging greater experimentation. The proposed changes would mark an early departure from Tim Cook's leadership approach as Apple faces mounting pressure to move faster in artificial intelligence and emerging consumer technology.

According to Bloomberg, Ternus, who succeeded Cook earlier this month, has discussed abandoning Apple's traditional spring and fall product-release cadence in favor of a more flexible launch strategy.
He is also reportedly exploring ways to reduce middle-management layers, allowing engineers to communicate more directly with senior executives and potentially shortening development cycles.
The changes may already be taking shape.

Over the past two weeks, Apple's hardware engineering division began eliminating several engineering program manager positions, affecting roughly half a dozen directors. The employees will reportedly have opportunities to secure alternative roles internally before departing.

The restructuring extends beyond hardware management. Apple has also reduced staffing across its Vision Pro and Siri teams, while cuts to Fitness+ have raised questions about the subscription service's future as its functionality increasingly overlaps with Apple's Health app.
Separately, the company reportedly considered eliminating approximately 5,000 AppleCare customer service positions over the summer before putting those plans on hold.
Taken together, the developments suggest Ternus is reevaluating both Apple's organizational structure and how quickly new products reach consumers.
The potential shift matters because Apple's tightly coordinated hardware and software ecosystem has historically relied on predictable release schedules, particularly for the iPhone.
Investors should watch whether faster development translates into meaningful improvements in Siri AI, more competitive emerging devices and shorter commercialization timelines.
Apple's upcoming product announcements and earnings commentary could offer early clues about how aggressively Ternus intends to reshape its operations.

The tradeoff is execution risk. Faster launches and leaner management could improve responsiveness, but compromising product reliability or disrupting established development processes could undermine the premium ecosystem supporting Apple's profitability.

title: New Apple CEO Makes Surprising Move After Tim Cook Exit
